motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Employee Policies and Procedures Manual for Bereavement Leave. Human Resource Manager Angela Valenzuela presented the item. The proposed amendment changes Funeral Leave to Bereavement Leave and brings the City's bereavement leave policy in compliance with the recently passed Senate Bill 63, which requires municipalities to provide at least three days of bereavement leave to all employees, including part-time workers, following the miscarriage or stillbirth of a child. Discussion ensued regarding which relatives to include as immediate family members and unpaid leave versus paid time off. 3. ADJOURN TO A CLOSED EXECUTIVE SESSION No closed session was held. Mayor Pro Tempore Love adjourned the work session at 6:42 p.m. 7:00 P.M. POLICY SESSION – CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS ELECTED OFFICIALS PRESENT: Councilmembers Donna Burnham, Colby Curtis, Jared Gray, Carolyn Love, and Brett Wright. Mayor Tom Westmoreland was excused. CITY STAFF PRESENT: Steve Mumford, Assistant City Administrator/Community Development Director; Robert Hobbs, Planning Manager; Senior Planner, Tayler Jensen; Fionnuala Kofoed, Director of Administrative Services/City Recorder; Chris Trusty, City Engineer; Jeremy Cook, City Attorney; Kimberly Ruesch, Finance Director; Zac Hilton, Streets and Storm Drain Manager; Angela Valenzuela, Human Resource Manager; Embret Fossum, UFA Battalion Chief; and B.J. Eccles, Sergeant. CITY STAFF PRESENT ELECTRONICALLY: Aaron Sanborn, Economic Development Director; Jeff Weber, Fleet and Facilities/Operations Director; Tyler Maffitt, Communications Manager; Brad Hickman, Parks and Recreation Director; Mack Straw, Public Utilities Manager; Michele Graves, Library Director; and Chas Glenn, Administrative Assistant. 4. CALL TO ORDER Mayor Pro Tempore Love called the policy session to order at 7:15 p.m. 5. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Councilmember Curtis led the Pledge of Allegiance. 6. INFORMATION ITEMS/UPCOMING EVENTS • Pony Express Days will take place June 1 through 4. To learn more, visit the redesigned City Events page on the Eagle Mountain City website. • Eagle Mountain residents are asked to voluntarily reduce their lawn watering during the spring and summer months. Due to Utah’s historic drought conditions, saving on water can not only help conserve the State’s water resources but also save residents money. This week, we are recommending residents water once per week. Follow the City's digital signs or social media for updated information. • Tooele Army Depot has communicated that the factors leading to large explosions in April should be curtailed during drier months later this year. If residents have concerns, they are encouraged to contact the Tooele Army Depot. • The start of new HAM Radio classes will begin on May 26. For more information, please reference the City calendar, or contact the Emergency Management Department staff. To receive City notifications, including emergency info, news events, and traffic alerts, sign up at emcity.org/notifyme. 7. INTRODUCTION 7.A. 2022 Eagle Mountain Rodeo Royalty Councilmember Gray stated Pony Express Events held their rodeo queen contest the previous week. He congratulated Queen Tristan Moulton, 1st Attendant Piper Maxwell, 2nd Attendant Kaycee Goodwin, Princess Rachel Whitehead, Princess 1st Attendant Hadley Warnick, and Princess 2nd Attendant Taytum Anderson 8. PUBLIC COMMENTS Mayor Pro Tempore Love opened public comment at 7:22 p.m. Tyler Shimakonis recognized the outgoing Youth Council members and participants and presented those in attendance with a certificate. In addition, he acknowledged and expressed appreciation to Garen Pabst, Adara Pabst, Emma Bird, Sedona Montano, Eliza Jensen, Lily Ratzlaff, and Davin Shimakonis for their assistance and participation in Youth Council meetings and events. Youth Council elections will be held Thursday and Friday at Cedar Valley and Rockwell High Schools and voting will be open at City Hall those evenings. Gabe Rolfe, a student attending Lakeview Academy, sent a letter to the City Council in April and was inadvertently excluded from being mentioned with the others at that time. Jill Jones submitted a written comment suggesting a small pool and fountain for a bird sanctuary be installed at the location of the old fire station near the Senior Citizens Center. Jason Robinson spoke about storing trailers on his property and receiving notices from Neighborhood Improvement. He requested to be allowed to store trailers as they have been there for twenty years. Jeff Marshall said he also has stored trailers on his property for 20 years and requested to be grandfathered into the standards at the time he moved to the City. Assistant City Administrator/Community Development Director Steve Mumford stated that he has appointments scheduled with Mr. Robinson and Mr. Marshall to discuss the situation. Mayor Pro Tempore Love closed public comment at 7:36 p.m. 9. CITY COUNCIL/MAYOR'S ITEMS Councilmember Curtis Councilmember Curtis thanked the meeting participants for their attendance. Councilmember Burnham Councilmember Burnham thanked the residents for attending both in-person and virtually. Mayor Pro Tempore Love Mayor Pro Tempore Love expressed appreciation to resident participants and those following water conservation guidelines. Councilmember Wright Councilmember Wright shared that he visited the Unified Fire Authority (UFA) fire training school and expressed his admiration and gratitude for firefighters and paramedics in our community. Councilmember Gray Councilmember Gray expressed gratitude to Senior Planner Tayler Jensen, other past City employees, Neighborhood Improvement Officers, and Tyler and Jennifer Shimakonis for their service. He inquired if 15-year-olds are allowed to be employed by the City. Human Resource Manager Angela Valenzuela said that due to restrictions on employing 15-year- olds, the City has elected to require employees to be a minimum of 16 years. She will provide Councilmember Gray with a list of available summer employment opportunities for youth. 10. APPOINTMENTS 10.A. Senior Citizens Advisory Council

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Consolidated Fee Schedule for New Asphalt Seal Coats, Road Closures, and Construction Water Fees. City Engineer Chris Trusty stated that further research found that Orem, Riverton, and Spanish Fork require a $1,000 minimum deposit and a rate based upon the length of the road closure. He recommended to implement a fee of $250 per lane per 1,000 feet for a collector road, $500 per lane per 1,000 feet for a minor arterial road, and $1,000 per lane per 1,000 feet for a major arterial road, along with a $1,000 deposit.
motions.motion: Councilmember Curtis moved to approve a resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending the Consolidated Fee Schedule for New Asphalt Seal Coats, Road Closures, and Construction Water Fees with the following amendments: 1. The addition of a $1,000 deposit; 2. The minimum fee for closure of a collector road per 1,000 feet per lane shall be $250 per day; 3. The minimum fee for closure of a minor arterial road per 1,000 feet per lane shall be $500 per day; and 4. The minimum fee for closure of a major arterial per 1,000 feet per lane shall be $1,000 per day. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion. motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Employee Policies and Procedures Manual for Bereavement Leave. Mayor Pro Tempore Love and Councilmember Curtis recommended including stepchildren as immediate family members. Discussion ensued regarding whether to include stepchildren and other additional family members as immediate family members qualifying for 40 hours of paid bereavement leave or to approve the amendment as drafted with deaths of other family members not included as immediate family granting 30 hours of paid bereavement leave with consideration of variance in the closeness of relationships on a personal basis, involvement with funeral planning, and concerns with cumulative time off and potential misuse of the policy.
motions.motion: Councilmember Curtis moved to approve a resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending the Eagle Mountain City Employee Policies and Procedures Manual for Bereavement Leave moving stepchild to the first paragraph, immediate family category. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
